principle: ATTACHMENT IS NOT A LOAD PATH — an attached relationship can remain geometrically present while transmitting zero force until slack reaches a taut threshold.

novelty.problem: tension-only relationship with constant attachment topology and slack-to-taut force activation
novelty.visible_mechanism: The same body-to-external-element tether is visible throughout. A sagging line carries no force while the body falls; near-taut geometry becomes eligible; zero slack acquires a straight tension axis; the COM path bends, overshoots and counter-swings under persistent tension; damping settles the body into a displaced equilibrium without custody transfer or an invented release.

source.title: Green Army Man

Distinct deployed-parachute/descent families establish a body-to-external-drag relationship while local body pose varies.
observed: The commissioned whole-sheet record covers the complete 576x720 selected sheet and all eight named families/previews.
Parachute/deployed-descent families visibly coexist with free-air and grounded families, establishing an external drag surface coupled to the body.
The source is a static sheet; source-authentic decisive-key chronology and exposure duration are unavailable.
